about: The lords of Xibalba want the boys to die at once in the ball game, but once more it is Xibalba that is beaten. They stop the boys from leaving and play with the boys' own ball. Then the lords set the stake: four bowls of flowers, a bunch each of red muchih, white muchit, yellow muchit and carinimac. The boys agree, play, and let themselves lose. The lords rejoice that for once they have won, and say the flowers are to be handed over that night. The boys are sent into Chaim Ha, the House of Blades, the second trial of Xibalba, where the blades are meant to cut them down; but the boys promise the blades the flesh of all the animals, and the blades stop moving and all go down together. In the night the boys call the ants, the Chai ants and the Chequen ants, and send them to fetch the flowers from the garden of Huncame and Vucub Came. The lords have warned the garden's guardians, two birds called Puhuyu, to keep watch all night. The birds sit in the branches crying their calls, Xpurpuvec and Puhuyu, and never notice the ants cutting the flowers and gnawing their own tails and wings. By dawn the four bowls are full. The boys bring them to the lords, who see their own flowers and go pale. The guardians are punished by having their mouths split, which is why the Purpuec bird has a split beak to this day. The ball game is played again, ends level, and is put off until the next morning.

sentences.t: Are ta cu xahauax chique ꜭaholab huzu ta xcam ri chiri chi cha, xe chacatah tah.
sentences.l: This (ta) then it-was-wanted to-them the-boys: quickly (ta) he-died the there at ball-court(?), they-were-brought-low (tah).
sentences.i: What was wanted for the boys, then, was that they should die quickly, there at the ball court (?), and be brought low.
sentences.n: The part opens with the words of 018's Are ta xahauax chiquech (018 U34), here with chique ꜭaholab. xahauax 'it was wanted': x- + ah 'want' + -auax, a passive (inferred, as in 018). chique ꜭaholab 'for the boys'. huzu 'quickly' (toggle jusuk, as published huzu before a word without c). xcam 'he died' is singular for the pair. ta and tah mark the wish: what the lords hoped for, not what happened. At the start Ximénez first wrote ri hun chi and struck it out, then wrote ri with a caret and chiri at the start of the next line; chiri 'there' is printed in place. chi cha: the manuscript has one a, and Brasseur prints chi chaa; cha may be the obsidian blade of 010 and 011, or chaa, the ball court of 018, written short. 'The ball court' is taken here because the next sentences are about the game (Brasseur 'dans le jeu de paume'; inferred). xe chacatah 'they were brought low', the passive in -atah of the earlier parts.

sentences.t: Mavi quehe; xa Xibalba xe chacatah chic cumal ꜭaholab.
sentences.l: Not thus; only Xibalba they-were-brought-low again by-them the-boys.
sentences.i: It was not so: it was Xibalba that was brought low again, by the boys.
sentences.n: Mavi quehe 'not so', the narrator's turn. xa Xibalba 'only Xibalba', that is, Xibalba and not the boys. xe chacatah chic 'they were brought low again'; chic 'again', after the game of the last part. cumal 'by them' (c- 'their' + umal), with ꜭaholab named after it.

sentences.t: “Ma ba quix bec, ix ꜭaholab. Coh chaah na; xa are ca ca coho ri ivech,” xvꜭhax cut ꜭaholab.
sentences.l: “Not (ba) you-go, you boys. We-play first; only this (ca) we-put the yours,” they-were-spoken-to then the-boys.
sentences.i: “Do not go, boys. Let us play first; and we shall put yours in play,” the boys were told.
sentences.n: The boys had just said Xa coh bec 'we are going' (end of 018). Ma ba quix bec 'do not go': ma 'not', ba the particle of urging, quix 'you (pl.)' + bec 'go'. In the manuscript ma ba looks like mabu (a and u are hard to tell apart in this hand) and is read with Brasseur's Ma-ba. Coh chaah na 'let us play first': coh, c- + oh 'we', chaah 'play (ball)', na 'first'. xa are ca ca coho ri ivech 'we shall put in yours': the manuscript has ca twice, where Brasseur prints one (ka coho); the first is taken as the ongoing c-, the second as ca 'we' (inferred). coho 'put' (coh 'put' + -o). ivech 'yours (pl.)' is the boys' ball, the same ball the lords refused at the end of 018 (Brasseur 'prenons maintenant la vôtre'). xvꜭhax 'they were told', the passive of ꜭha 'speak', here without the plural e.

sentences.t: “Vꜩ bala,” xeꜭha cut.
sentences.l: “Good bala,” they-said then.
sentences.i: “Very well,” they said.
sentences.n: Vꜩ bala 'very well', the house rendering. The boys agree.

sentences.t: Are cu xoc ri qui quic, ta xcah cu chaah.
sentences.l: This then it-entered the their rubber, when it-went-down then the-play.
sentences.i: So it was their rubber ball that went into play, and the game began.
sentences.n: ri qui quic 'their rubber', the boys' ball (quic 'blood' and 'rubber', as in 018; toggle kik'). xoc 'it entered' (oc 'enter'), here into play. xcah cu chaah 'the game went down': cah 'go down' (toggle qaj), as again in ¶10, where the game starts over (xcah chaah); 'the game began' is inferred. Brasseur takes it the other way: 'ce qui mit aussitôt fin à la partie'.

sentences.t: Catecut ta xqui choi qui chacon: “Naquipa chi ca chaco?” xeꜭha Xibalba.
sentences.l: Then when they-counted(?) their beating(?): “What (chi) we-win?” they-said Xibalba.
sentences.i: Then they counted up the defeats (?): “What shall we win?” said Xibalba.
sentences.n: xqui choi 'they counted' is not otherwise known; the sense follows Brasseur's 'ayant compté' (a guess; the toggle respells the letters). qui chacon and chaco are both from chac 'defeat, win' (009, 010): chaco 'win, beat' (-o, the ending of a transitive verb), and chacon, with -on, the thing won, which in this part is the stake the lords claim: qui chacon ahauab 'what the lords have won' (¶4), ca chacon 'what we have won' (¶5, ¶8). Here Brasseur has 'leurs défaites', the games they had lost; either may be meant (inferred). Brasseur's note: chaco 'vaincre, combattre, humilier dans un combat', and also 'battre au jeu, tromper, tricher'. chi ca chaco: ca 'we'. Naquipa 'what' (naqui + pa). The lords now set a wager.

sentences.t: “He na qui cut,” xa xeꜭha ꜭaholab.
sentences.l: “Go(?) first(?) (qui) then,” only they-said the-boys.
sentences.i: “Go on, then (?),” was all the boys said.
sentences.n: A doubtful line. He is taken as the 'go' of 010 and of 018's He bala 'go on, then' (inferred); na 'first, now'; qui is not clear (perhaps k- + i- 'you (pl.)', perhaps 'they'). The established text follows the house reading of the tags, by which xa xeꜭha ꜭaholab 'only the boys said' closes the words before it, so the line is the boys'. Brasseur reads He na qui cut … cah ꜩel coꜩih as one speech of Xibalba: 'Qu'ils s'en aillent donc à l'heure même, ces jeunes gens, et qu'entre temps ils nous apportent quatre vases de fleurs'. Either reading can be got from the words.

sentences.t: “Xa ca cha ca cah cah ꜩel coꜩih,” xeꜭha Xibalba.
sentences.l: “Only (ca) say(?) (ca) we-want four bowl flower,” they-said Xibalba.
sentences.i: “All we want (?) is four bowls of flowers,” said Xibalba.
sentences.n: The first words are a doubtful reading. The manuscript has xacachara cah | cah ꜩel, and the fourth letter of chaca could be r; it is printed Xa ca cha ca cah, a doubtful division (Brasseur xa-cucha ca kah cah tzel cotzih). cha may be the 'say' of earlier parts. ca cah is taken as ca + cah 'we want' (cah: c- 'we' + ah 'want', the verb of 014's chi cah; inferred), with the next cah the numeral 'four' (toggle kaj). cah ꜩel coꜩih 'four bowls of flowers' is clear: ꜩel 'bowl', the bowl of Ah Raxa Ꜩel in the litany of 001; coꜩih 'flower' (toggle kotz'i'j, the known word, the tz' supplied on the plain ligature, as in 015–018).

sentences.t: “Vꜩ bala. Naquipa chi coꜩihal?” xeꜭha ꜭaholab chique Xibalba.
sentences.l: “Good bala. What of flowers?” they-said the-boys to-them Xibalba.
sentences.i: “Very well. Which flowers?” the boys said to Xibalba.
sentences.n: Two speeches under one tag: the boys agree, then ask. chi coꜩihal 'of flowers', 'what kind of flowers': coꜩih + -al, the ending of a noun of kind or collection (inferred). chique Xibalba 'to Xibalba'.

sentences.t: “Huticab cacamuchih, huticab zaqui muchit, huticab cana muchit, huticab carinimac,” xeꜭha Xibalba.
sentences.l: “One-bunch(?) red-muchih, one-bunch(?) white muchit, one-bunch(?) yellow muchit, one-bunch(?) carinimac,” they-said Xibalba.
sentences.i: “A bunch of red muchih, a bunch of white muchit, a bunch of yellow muchit, a bunch of carinimac,” said Xibalba.
sentences.n: Four flowers, one for each bowl. huticab is a doubtful reading: the manuscript looks like huhcab with the dot of an i over the second h, a t written like h, as elsewhere in this hand; it is read with Brasseur's huticab. It is taken as hu(n) 'one' + a measure word, 'a bunch', after Brasseur's 'un bouquet' (inferred; the toggle respells the letters). The flowers: caca 'red' + muchih (written as one word); zaqui 'white' + muchit; cana muchit, taken as ꜫana 'yellow', written with plain c (Brasseur gana; toggle q'ana, the colour word being certain here, as plain-c acab gives aq'ab'); and carinimac, not divided and not explained. The manuscript has muchih for the first and muchit for the second and third (Brasseur muchih, muchih, muchit); printed as written. Brasseur's note says these flowers are all of the kind called chipilin in Central America, a Nahuatl word. The names of the flowers are kept in the English, with their colours translated.

sentences.t: “Vꜩ bala,” xeꜭha cut ꜭaholab.
sentences.l: “Good bala,” they-said then the-boys.
sentences.i: “Very well,” said the boys.
sentences.n: The boys accept the wager.

sentences.t: Ta xcah cut qui cha; hunam qui chucab, ꜩaꜩ pu qui cha ri ꜭaholab; xa cu qui rvꜩ qui ꜭux ta xqui ya quib chi chacatahic ri ꜭaholab.
sentences.l: Then it-went-down then their play(?); equal their strength, many also their play(?) the boys; only then their its-goodness their heart when they-gave themselves to being-brought-low the boys.
sentences.i: Then their game began (?): their strength was equal, and many, too, were the boys' plays (?); but the boys were at ease in their hearts as they gave themselves up to be beaten.
sentences.n: A hard sentence. Ta xcah cut qui cha is read with ¶1's xcah cu chaah 'the game began', taking cha as chaah 'play' written with one a (as 018's chahoc 'to play'; inferred). Brasseur takes cha as 'lances' here ('Alors descendirent leurs (gardes armés de) lances'), and his footnote on ¶4's chire cha says that in this passage cha means in turn 'say', 'lance' and 'lancer' ('le mot cha signifie alternativement le verbe dire ou parler, lance et lancier'). A small blot after qui cha on the page hides nothing. hunam qui chucab 'equal their strength' (hunam 'alike, equal'; chucab 'strength', toggle chuq'ab'). ꜩaꜩ pu qui cha ri ꜭaholab 'many too (were) the boys' plays (?)': ꜩaꜩ 'many, thick'; pu 'also'. xa cu qui rvꜩ qui ꜭux 'but their hearts were good (at ease)': rvꜩ is r- 'its' + vꜩ 'good', after qui, a doubling not otherwise seen (Brasseur r'utzqui qux, 'tranquille était l'âme'; inferred). xqui ya quib chi chacatahic 'they gave themselves to being beaten': ya 'give', quib 'themselves', chacatahic the verbal noun of chacatah. The boys lose on purpose.

sentences.t: Que quicot cut ri Xibalba ta xe chacatahic: “Vꜩ mix ca bano; nabe mixe ca chaco,” xeꜭha Xibalba.
sentences.l: They-rejoice then the Xibalba when they-were-brought-low: “Good we-have-just done-it; first we-have-just-them beaten,” they-said Xibalba.
sentences.i: Then Xibalba rejoiced, when the boys were beaten: “We have done well: for once we have beaten them,” said Xibalba.
sentences.n: Que quicot 'they rejoice', que, c- (the ongoing) + e 'they'. ta xe chacatahic 'when they were brought low', the boys. mix ca bano 'we have just done (it)': mi 'just now' + x- + ca 'we' + bano 'do'. nabe mixe ca chaco 'first we have beaten them': mixe is mi + x- + e 'them'; nabe 'first', the first time they have won (Brasseur 'tout d'abord', 'pris au piége').

sentences.t: “Apa xchi be qui cama vi ri coꜩih?” xeꜭha chi qui ꜭux.
sentences.l: “Where shall go they-take there the flowers?” they-said in their heart.
sentences.i: “Where will they go to get the flowers?” they said in their hearts.
sentences.n: Apa 'where'. xchi be 'shall go': the future xchi-. qui cama 'they take, fetch': cama is the 'take' verb with plain c (Brasseur qama; toggle kama by the letters, as published; the 'take' verb is still an open question). vi points to the place. chi qui ꜭux 'in their hearts': the lords say it to themselves.

sentences.t: “Quiꜩih ta acab chi ia ri ca coꜩih; ca chacom puch,” xe vꜭhax puch ꜭaholab Hunahpu, Xbalanque rumal Xibalba.
sentences.l: “Truly (ta) night let-be-given the our flowers; our won-thing also,” they-were-spoken-to also the-boys Hunahpu, Xbalanque by Xibalba.
sentences.i: “Truly, tonight our flowers are to be given to us; they are what we have won,” the boys Hunahpu and Xbalanque were told by Xibalba.
sentences.n: Quiꜩih ta 'truly'. acab 'night', with the plain c the hand shows (Brasseur agab); the toggle restores aq'ab', the house word aꜫab, as 015 and 016 printed acab. 018 printed aꜫab for what may be the same letter; the two parts differ, and a house decision is wanted. chi ia 'let (them) be given': chi of wishing + ia, the 'give' verb written with Ximénez's i for y (MS chiia; Brasseur ch'y ya), with no doer named (toggle ya). ca chacom puch 'and our won thing': chac 'win' + -om, perhaps a participle 'won' (inferred; Brasseur 'nous sommes les gagnants maintenant'). xe vꜭhax 'they were told'.

sentences.t: “Vꜩ bala; acaba chi cut coh chaahic,” xeꜭha cut, ta xe pixaban quib.
sentences.l: “Good bala; at-night(?) again then we-play,” they-said then, when they-counselled themselves.
sentences.i: “Very well; at night (?), then, we shall play again,” they said, and they took counsel together.
sentences.n: acaba is a doubtful reading in the manuscript. It is taken as acab 'night' + -a, with plain c (Brasseur Agaba, 'Cette nuit également'; toggle aq'ab'a). The game in fact starts again after dawn (¶10), so the sense may be 'early, at daybreak'; in modern K'iche' aq'ab' is also used of the early morning (inferred). chi cut is chic 'again' + cut (toggle chik). coh chaahic 'we play': coh 'we', chaahic 'playing'. xe pixaban quib 'they counselled one another': pixab 'counsel' + -an, with quib 'themselves' (inferred; Brasseur 's'avisant mutuellement'; toggle pixab'an).

sentences.t: Cate chi cut ta xe oc chi ꜭaholab pa Chaim Ha, v cab tihobal Xibalba.
sentences.l: Then again then when they-entered again the-boys in Chaim House, its second trial Xibalba.
sentences.i: After that the boys went in again, into Chaim Ha, the House of Blades (?), the second trial of Xibalba.
sentences.n: Cate chi cut 'then again then': chi is chic without its c, twice in this line (toggle chik). Chaim Ha is the house of 011's list, 'the House of Blades (?)': cha 'blade, obsidian point' + -im + ha 'house'; 'House of Blades' is inferred (Brasseur here 'la Maison des Lances', his text Chàim-ha; in 011 his introduction has 'la Maison des Lances d'Obsidienne'). v cab tihobal 'its second trial': v cab 'second' (as 018's v cab culel), tihobal 'trial' (010, 018). The Dark House was the first (018).

sentences.t: Are ta cut xahauax chic xe catacox tah rumal cha chanim tah, chi qui ꜭux; xe cam tah, chi qui ꜭux.
sentences.l: This (ta) then it-was-wanted again: they-were-cut(?) (tah) by blade quickly (tah), in their heart; they-died (tah), in their heart.
sentences.i: Again it was wanted that they be cut down by the blades, quickly, as the lords had it in mind; that they die, as they had it in mind.
sentences.n: The opening words of ¶1 again, now for the blades. xe catacox tah 'that they be cut': catacox is taken as ꜫat 'cut' (as 011's xcat) + -ac + -ox, a passive, written with plain c (Brasseur gatacox, 'qu'ils fussent tués par les lanciers'; toggle q'atakox, the q' after Brasseur's g and the sense, as 011; inferred). rumal cha 'by the blade(s)': cha is the obsidian blade (Brasseur's note: cha for chai, 'lance ou lancier, flèche ou archer'; chai 'le couteau d'obsidienne'). chanim 'quickly'. tah marks the wish three times. chi qui ꜭux … chi qui ꜭux 'in their heart', twice: a couplet of the lords' intention.

sentences.t: Ma cu xe camic.
sentences.l: Not then they-died.
sentences.i: But they did not die.
sentences.n: Ma cu 'but not'. xe camic 'they died' (cam 'die' + -ic).

sentences.t: Ta xeꜭha chire cha, ta xqui pixabah: “Are ive ri ronohel v tiohil chicop,” xeꜭha chire cha.
sentences.l: Then they-spoke to-it blade, then they-charged-it: “This yours the all its-flesh animal,” they-said to-it blade.
sentences.i: Then they spoke to the blades, and gave them their charge: “Yours shall be the flesh of every animal,” they said to the blades.
sentences.n: chire cha 'to the blade(s)': chire 'to it' (chi + r- + e), singular, for the blades together. xqui pixabah 'they charged them' (pixab 'counsel' + -ah; 010, 015). Are ive 'yours (it is)': ive 'yours (pl.)'. v tiohil chicop 'the flesh of animals': in the manuscript the t is written like an h (vhohil) and is read with Brasseur's u tiohil (tiohil 'flesh, meat'). Brasseur's note: 'Par des promesses ils séduisent leurs gardiens'. The tag xeꜭha chire cha repeats the opening: the speech is framed by it.

sentences.t: Ma cu xe zilab chic; xa hun cah chi vi cha ronohel.
sentences.l: Not then they-moved again; only one it-went-down (chi) there blade all.
sentences.i: And they did not move any more: all the blades went down together, as one.
sentences.n: xe zilab 'they moved' (zilab 'stir, move', as earlier; toggle silab'); chic 'any more'. xa hun cah … ronohel 'only one went down … all', the blades lowered all together (Brasseur 'unanimement ils baissèrent leurs armes'; inferred). cah is 'go down' (toggle qaj), as in ¶1 and ¶3. chi vi: chi is not clear here (perhaps chic 'again', its c not written), and the toggle keeps the letters; vi points to the place.

sentences.t: Are cut e ꜭo chi chiri pa Chaim Ha chacab, ta xqui ziquih ronohel zanic: “Chai zanic, Chequen zanic, quix petoc, quix oho ivonohel; oh i cama ronohel v vach coꜩih qui chacon ahauab.”
sentences.l: This then they were still there in Chaim House at-night, when they-called all ants: “Chai ants, Chequen ants, you-come, you-come-here all-of-you; we(?) you-take all its-face flower their-won-thing lords.”
sentences.i: And while they were still there in Chaim Ha, in the night, they called all the ants: “Chai ants, Chequen ants, come, come here, all of you: take for us (?) every bloom of the flowers that the lords have won.”
sentences.n: e ꜭo chi chiri 'they were still there': e ꜭo 'they are', with the g-shaped letter read ꜭ; chi is chic 'still' (toggle chik). chacab 'at night': chi + acab, with plain c, a doubtful reading (Brasseur ch'agab; toggle chaq'ab', as published). xqui ziquih 'they called' (ziquih 'call'). zanic 'ants' (014). Brasseur's note: zanic is the general word for the ant; the Chequen zanic is a big ant that goes about at night and cuts the stems of tender plants and flowers 'comme avec des ciseaux', called zanpopo in Guatemalan Spanish. Chai is taken as chai 'obsidian' (Brasseur's note on cha above; his French 'Fourmis tranchantes', cutting ants); the names are kept in the English (toggle Chay, Cheken). quix petoc, quix oho 'come, come here (you pl.)': a couplet; the manuscript clearly has petoc where Brasseur prints pene. oho 'come here' as 017 and 018 (inferred). ivonohel 'all of you' (iv- + onohel, as conohel). oh i cama is written as one word (ohicama), divided with Brasseur's oh y qama: oh 'we', perhaps 'for us', + i- 'you (pl.)' + cama 'take' (inferred; Brasseur 'allez chercher'). v vach coꜩih 'the face of the flowers', their blooms (vach 'face', also 'fruit'). qui chacon ahauab 'the lords' won thing', the stake of ¶2. Brasseur prints chi chacon here ('que nous ont dit les princes'); the manuscript has qui (image rechecked), and the establishment log is silent.

sentences.t: “Vꜩ bala,” xeꜭha cut.
sentences.l: “Good bala,” they-said then.
sentences.i: “Very well,” they said.
sentences.n: The ants answer.

sentences.t: Ta xe be cu ri zanic conohel, e camol coꜩih v ticon Huncame, Vvcub Came.
sentences.l: Then they-went then the ants all-of-them, they takers flower its-planting Huncame, Vucub Came.
sentences.i: So all the ants went off, to take the flowers from the garden of Huncame and Vucub Came.
sentences.n: e camol coꜩih 'they (were) takers of the flowers': camol, the agent noun of the 'take' verb, with plain c (Brasseur qamol; toggle k'amol, as published in 018). v ticon 'its planting, garden': in the manuscript the t is written like an h (hcon), read with Brasseur's ticon; tic 'plant' (017) + -on (inferred; Brasseur 'jardin'; toggle tikon). Huncame, Vvcub Came, the two chief lords (009); Vvcub is printed as 018 (v and u look alike in this hand).

sentences.t: Mier oc cut chi qui pixabah chahal qui coꜩih ri Xibalba: “La qui chivila ca coꜩih; mi ya chi elecaxic rumal ri mixe ca chaco ri ꜭaholab.
sentences.l: Just-now already then (chi) they-charged guardian their-flowers the Xibalba: “(La) you watch-it our-flowers; not give to being-stolen by the we-have-just-them beaten the boys.
sentences.i: Xibalba had already given their charge to the guardians of their flowers: “Watch over our flowers; do not let them be stolen by these boys we have beaten.
sentences.n: The lords' charge runs on into the next unit; it is cut at its question. Mier oc 'already, beforehand': mier 'just now' + oc 'already' (Brasseur 'D'avance'). chi qui pixabah 'they charged': chi is the particle before a verb, not rendered. chahal 'guardian, keeper' (013's Chahal Echa), from chah 'guard'. La is not clear (perhaps the respectful la of earlier parts; Brasseur 'Quant à vous'). qui chivila 'look at it, you (pl.)': ch- (command) + iv- 'you (pl.)' + il 'see' + -a; qui before it is not clear (perhaps c- + i- 'you (pl.)'). mi ya 'do not give, do not let'. chi elecaxic 'to be stolen': elec 'steal' + -ax, the passive, + -ic, written with plain c (Brasseur elegaxic; toggle eleq'axik, the known word, the q' after Brasseur's g and the sense). mixe ca chaco 'we have beaten them', as in ¶3.

sentences.t: Ana vi xpe vi rilo ca chacon cumal? Mahabi. Chi varah hun acab.”
sentences.l: Where(?) (vi) it-came there he-sees-it our-won-thing by-them? There-is-not. You-watch one night.”
sentences.i: From where could they come to see what we have won? Nowhere. Keep watch the whole night.”
sentences.n: Ana vi is the word of 016 (there 'perhaps', a guess); here Mahabi 'there is not' answers it, so it is taken as 'where?' (Brasseur 'Où donc'; inferred). xpe vi rilo 'from where did it come that he see': xpe 'it came', rilo 'he sees it' (r- + il + -o). ca chacon 'our won thing', the flowers the lords claim. cumal 'by them'. Chi varah 'keep watch, you (pl.)': ch- + i- + varah 'keep watch' (016, inferred; Brasseur 'Veillez'). hun acab 'one night', all night, with plain c (toggle aq'ab').

sentences.t: “Vꜩ bala,” xeꜭha cut.
sentences.l: “Good bala,” they-said then.
sentences.i: “Very well,” they said.
sentences.n: The guardians agree.

sentences.t: Ma cu xquina ri chahal ticon.
sentences.l: Not then they-felt-it the guardian planting.
sentences.i: But the guardians of the garden noticed nothing.
sentences.n: xquina 'they felt, noticed': x- + qui 'they' + na 'feel', written as one word (na, as nao 'feel' in 004, 006, 007 and 012; toggle xkina). chahal ticon 'the guardians of the garden' (ticon written hcon, as above).

sentences.t: Xaloc chi qui racuh qui chi chu cab tac che ticon puch;
sentences.l: In-vain (chi) they-scrape their-mouths at-its-arm the-various tree planting also;
sentences.i: All for nothing they cried out at the top of their voices in the branches of the garden trees;
sentences.n: Xaloc 'in vain, for nothing' (015, inferred), with plain c (Brasseur xalog). qui racuh qui chi 'they scrape their mouths', they cry out with all their strength (the racuh … vchi of 005–007; Brasseur 'criant de toutes leurs forces'; inferred). chu cab tac che 'on the arms of the trees', the branches: chu (chi + v- 'its') + cab 'arm, hand' with plain c (Brasseur gab; toggle q'ab') + tac, the plural word. ticon puch 'of the garden also' (ticon written hcon again).

sentences.t: que be chacala chiri, xavi xere chi qui ꜭhabeh ri qui bix: “Xpurpuvec, Xpurpuvec,” ꜭha ri hun ta choquic.
sentences.l: they-go perched(?) there, just so (chi) they-utter the their-song: “Xpurpuvec, Xpurpuvec,” says the one when crying.
sentences.i: they went about perched (?) there, uttering the same song over and over: “Xpurpuvec, Xpurpuvec,” the one said as it cried.
sentences.n: que be 'they go'. chacala is not otherwise known: perhaps the chac of chacabal 'what people stand by' (house table), 'standing, perched' (a guess; Brasseur 'cheminant sur leurs jambes'; toggle by the letters). xavi xere 'just so, only this'. qui ꜭhabeh 'they speak, utter': the g-shaped letter is read ꜭh (Brasseur chabeh); ꜭhab 'speak' + -eh (inferred; toggle ch'ab'ej). bix 'song'. Xpurpuvec: the manuscript writes the second one xpurpu- | uec across the line, u and v alike; printed as the first. Brasseur's note calls the two cries night watchmen's calls and reads them as phrases, x-pur pu-veh, 'it has entered into the night', and apparently Puhuyu as pu huyu 'on the mountain' (the OCR is damaged); his reading is a guess and the calls are kept as written. ꜭha ri hun 'said the one': the g-shaped letter again. choquic 'crying, singing', of a bird's call: ch- + oꜫ 'cry' + -ic, with plain c (Brasseur ch'ogic, his note 'le chant des oiseaux, le cri des bêtes'; toggle choq'ik, as 017).

sentences.t: “Puhuyu, Puhuyu,” cha chic ta choquic.
sentences.l: “Puhuyu, Puhuyu,” says again when crying.
sentences.i: “Puhuyu, Puhuyu,” went the other in turn, as it cried.
sentences.n: cha chic 'says in turn': cha, the 'say' root written with plain ch as in earlier parts (toggle by the letters), + chic 'again, in turn'. The other bird answers the first. Puhuyu is also the birds' name (next unit).

sentences.t: Ri Puhuyu v bi e caib chi chahal ticon v ticon Huncame, Vvcub Came.
sentences.l: The Puhuyu its-name they two (chi) guardian planting, its-planting Huncame, Vucub Came.
sentences.i: Puhuyu was the name of the two guardians of the garden, the garden of Huncame and Vucub Came.
sentences.n: Puhuyu is kept as a name. Brasseur's note: the watchers become night birds in the tale, one called Purpuek and the other a kind of owl (the note is damaged in the OCR). e caib 'the two of them' (caib 'two'). chi chahal 'as guardians' (chi not rendered). ticon v ticon 'of the garden, the garden of …': the word is written twice, hcon vhcon, on one line of the page (image rechecked), the second with v- 'its', so it reads as an apposition, not a slip at a line break; Brasseur prints only one ticon (chahal ticon Hun-Came), and the establishment log is silent. ticon is written hcon both times, as above.

sentences.t: Ma cu ca quina ri zanic elecai qui chahem, ca bolovic, ca tucuvic e rai coꜩih, ri ca be ca tova vloc coꜩih chuvi che, re ca zicou cuꜭ chuxe che ri coꜩih.
sentences.l: Not then they-feel the ants stealing their-guarded-thing, swarming(?), cutting(?) they its-...(?) flower, who go they-carry hither flower on-top-of tree, (re) they-gather(?) with-them at-foot-of tree the flower.
sentences.i: But they did not notice the ants stealing what they were guarding, swarming (?) and cutting (?) among the flowers (?), carrying the flowers off up the trees, and gathering (?) them at the foot of the trees.
sentences.n: Much here is doubtful. ca quina 'they feel, notice', the ongoing form of xquina (written ca quina, two words). elecai qui chahem 'stealing their guarded thing': elecai, a doubtful reading, from elec 'steal' with -ai, plain c (Brasseur elegai, 'dérobant'; toggle eleq'ai, inferred); chahem, chah 'guard' + -em, 'what is guarded' (inferred; Brasseur 'ce qui était commis à leur garde'). ca bolovic, ca tucuvic: two -vic verbs, a pair; 'swarming' and 'cutting' follow Brasseur ('allant et revenant en troupes innombrables', 'coupant') and are guesses. In ca tucuvic the letters are doubtful (Brasseur tuguvic); the toggle respells them. e rai coꜩih is not understood: rai is perhaps r- 'its' + a noun (Brasseur 'les plates bandes de fleurs', the beds), or the rai 'want' of 012 ('those who want the flowers'); left as '(?)'. ca be ca tova vloc 'they go carrying (them) hither': tova 'carry' (Brasseur 'portaient'; inferred; toggle towa). chuvi che … chuxe che 'on top of the trees … at the foot of the trees': a couplet. re ca zicou cuꜭ: re is perhaps 'their teeth' (r- 'its' + e 'tooth', for the ants taken together), the ants' jaws, as Brasseur in the next lines ('les dents'); zicou 'gather (?)', with plain c (Brasseur ziqou, which he renders 'répandaient une douce odeur', the flowers giving off their scent; a guess either way); cuꜭ 'with them', the g-shaped letter read ꜭ.

sentences.t: Xa quehe chi qui racuh qui chi ri chahalib; mana re ca qui nao ca ꜭux qui he, ca ꜭux qui xic.
sentences.l: Only thus (chi) they-scrape their-mouths the guardians; not teeth(?) they-feel gnawing(?) their-tails, gnawing(?) their-wings.
sentences.i: So the guardians just went on crying out, and did not feel the teeth (?) gnawing (?) at their tails, gnawing (?) at their wings.
sentences.n: chahalib 'guardians': chahal + the plural -ib (as -ab). mana 'not'. re is taken as 'teeth' (r- + e), after Brasseur 'les dents qui sciaient' (inferred). ca qui nao 'they feel it': ca, the ongoing, + qui 'they' + nao 'feel'. ca ꜭux qui he, ca ꜭux qui xic 'gnawing their tails, gnawing their wings', a couplet: the g-shaped letter is read ꜭ (Brasseur cux); ꜭux is the letters of ꜭux 'heart', here a verb 'gnaw, saw' after Brasseur ('étant à scier leurs queues, étant à scier leurs ailes'; inferred; toggle k'ux by the letters). he 'tail' (je'), xic 'wing' (010's vxic). Brasseur says in his note that there is an allusion here he does not understand.

sentences.t: Are ca quirixic coꜩih, ca ca cah vloc, re ca zicouic, re ca be ca tova vloc.
sentences.l: This being-loosed(?) flower, (ca) coming-down hither, teeth(?) gathering(?), teeth(?) go carrying hither.
sentences.i: All the while the flowers were being cut loose (?): coming down, gathered (?) in the ants' jaws (?), carried off in their jaws (?).
sentences.n: ca quirixic coꜩih 'the flowers are being loosed': quir 'untie, loosen' + -ix, the passive, + -ic (inferred; Brasseur 'c'était une moisson de fleurs'). ca ca cah vloc 'coming down hither': the manuscript has cacacah (Brasseur ca cu kah uloc); divided ca ca cah, the second ca not clear (inferred); cah 'go down' (toggle qaj). re ca zicouic, re ca be ca tova vloc: re and zicou as in the last unit (doubtful); Brasseur 'que leurs dents descendaient et que leurs dents transportaient tout odoriférantes'. In the margin beside re ca zicouic a large X in dark ink is a later reader's mark and is not followed.

sentences.t: Libah chi cut xnoh cahib ꜩel coꜩih; tiquitoh chi cut ta xzaquiric.
sentences.l: Instantly then it-filled four bowl flower; full already then when it-dawned.
sentences.i: In no time the four bowls of flowers were filled, and they were full by the time it dawned.
sentences.n: Libah chi 'in an instant', as 010 and 018; Brasseur writes Libahchi as one word. xnoh 'it was filled' (noh 'fill'; toggle xnoj). tiquitoh 'full, brimming' (Brasseur 'tout pleins'; inferred): in the manuscript the t is written like an h (hquitoh), read with Brasseur's tiquitoh. chi cut is chic 'already' + cut (Brasseur chicut; toggle chik). xzaquiric 'it dawned' (zac 'white, light' + -ir + -ic; 010's zaquiric).

sentences.t: Catecut ta xul zamahel taconel: “Que petoc,” ca ꜭha ahau; “huzuc chi qui cam vla ri ca chacon,” xe vꜭhax cut ꜭaholab.
sentences.l: Then when it-arrived messenger one-sent: “They-come,” says lord; “quickly let they-bring hither the our-won-thing,” they-were-spoken-to then the-boys.
sentences.i: Then the messenger came, the one sent: “Let them come,” says the lord; “let them bring here at once what we have won,” the boys were told.
sentences.n: zamahel taconel 'messenger, one sent', a pair (017; the manuscript divides ta- | conel across the line; Brasseur's OCR is damaged here). The messenger gives the lord's words, with ca ꜭha ahau 'says the lord': the g-shaped letter read ꜭ, ca the ongoing (toggle ka ch'a). Que petoc 'let them come': que, c- + e 'they', petoc 'come'. huzuc chi qui cam vla 'quickly let them bring here': chi of wishing; cam 'take, bring', with plain c (Brasseur qam; toggle k'am, as 015–017); vla 'hither'. ri ca chacon 'what we have won', the flowers (Brasseur 'ce dont nous avons parlé').

sentences.t: “Vꜩ bala,” xeꜭha cut.
sentences.l: “Good bala,” they-said then.
sentences.i: “Very well,” they said.
sentences.n: The boys answer.

sentences.t: Qui tique laon cu ri coꜩih cahib ꜩel; ta xe bec, ta xe opon cu chi qui vach ahau, ahauab, cu caam coꜩih ꜫuz v vach.
sentences.l: Their full(?) heaped(?) then the flowers four bowls; then they-went, then they-arrived then at their-face lord, lords; he-receives(?) flower, delight(?) its-face.
sentences.i: Full and heaped up (?) were the flowers, four bowls of them; then they went, and came before the lord and the lords, and he took the flowers, a delight (?) to see.
sentences.n: Qui tique laon is not understood. In the manuscript the t is written like an h (quihque laon) and is read with Brasseur's Qui tique laon; tique is taken with the tiquitoh 'full' of ¶7 and laon as 'heaped' (both guesses; Brasseur passes over the words, 'Ils allèrent ensuite chercher les quatre vases de fleurs'); the toggle respells the letters. cu ri looks like cari in the manuscript and is read with Brasseur's curi. ta xe bec, ta xe opon 'then they went, then they arrived': opon, arriving away from the speaker. chi qui vach ahau, ahauab 'before the lord, the lords'. cu caam 'he takes, receives': cu, c- + v- 'he' (Brasseur c'u caam, 'ceux-ci prirent'); caam is the kaam 'carry, take' of 014 (inferred; toggle by the letters). ꜫuz v vach 'pleasing (is) its face': ꜫuz is written with the q-shaped letter, as in 015 and 017 (a doubtful reading), here in 015's sense 'delight' after Brasseur 'dont l'aspect faisait plaisir' (a guess).

sentences.t: Quehe cut xe chacatah vi Xibalba;
sentences.l: Thus then they-were-brought-low there Xibalba;
sentences.i: So it was that Xibalba was brought low:
sentences.n: xe chacatah vi 'they were brought low there', the formula of earlier parts (012).

sentences.t: xa zanic xqui tac ri ꜭaholab; xa hun acabil xqui chap zanic ta qui ya pa ꜩel.
sentences.l: only ants they-sent the boys; only one night they-caught-it ants when they-put in bowl.
sentences.i: it was only ants that the boys had sent; in a single night the ants took the flowers and put them in the bowls.
sentences.n: xqui tac 'they sent' (tac 'send'). xa hun acabil 'in only one night': acab 'night' + -il, written with plain c (Brasseur agabil; toggle aq'ab'il). xqui chap 'they seized it, took it' (chap 'seize'). ta qui ya pa ꜩel 'when they put (them) into the bowl': ya 'give, put'; ꜩel singular for the four bowls.

sentences.t: Quehe cut xe zaccah e ri conohel Xibalba, zacbu e qui vach rumal ri coꜩih.
sentences.l: Thus then they-went-pale(?) they the all-of-them Xibalba, white(?) they their-faces because-of the flowers.
sentences.i: And so all of Xibalba went white, their faces pale because of the flowers.
sentences.n: xe zaccah e 'they turned white': the manuscript writes xezaccahe as one word, divided with Brasseur's x-e zakcah e; zac 'white' + cah, a verb of becoming (inferred; Brasseur 'changèrent de couleur'; the toggle supplies the q of zac only). zacbu e qui vach 'pale their faces': zac 'white' + -bu (not otherwise known; Brasseur 'leurs faces pâlirent'; inferred). e 'they', the plural word, twice. The lords see their own flowers.

sentences.t: Catecut xqui tac ri chahal coꜩih: “Naquipa rumal mix ia ca coꜩih chi elecaxic? Are ca coꜩih vae ca vilo,” xe vꜭhax chahal.
sentences.l: Then they-sent-for the guardian flower: “What because-of you-have-just given our-flowers to being-stolen? This our-flowers here I-see-it,” they-were-spoken-to guardian.
sentences.i: Then they sent for the guardians of the flowers: “Why have you let our flowers be stolen? These are our own flowers I see here,” the guardians were told.
sentences.n: xqui tac 'they sent (for)'. Naquipa rumal 'why', 'for what reason'. mix ia 'you (pl.) have given': mi + ix 'you (pl.)' + ia 'give' with Ximénez's i for y (MS mi | xia; Brasseur m'yx ya; toggle mix ya). chi elecaxic 'to be stolen', as in ¶5. vae 'here'. ca vilo 'I see it': ca, the ongoing, + v- 'I' (before a vowel) + il 'see' + -o, as 017's ca vilo (toggle ka wilo); one lord speaks for the rest. Brasseur reads 'we' (kav'ilo, 'que nous voyons'). xe vꜭhax chahal 'the guardians were told': a heavy blot follows chahal on the page, and nothing seems lost under it (Brasseur x-e uchax chahal).

sentences.t: “Ma ba xca nao, at ahau; mi na re xcuyu ca he,” xeꜭha cut.
sentences.l: “Not (ba) we-felt-it, you lord; not(?) even(?) (re) it-was-spared(?) our-tails,” they-said then.
sentences.i: “We noticed nothing, lord; not even our tails were spared (?),” they said.
sentences.n: Ma ba xca nao 'we did not feel it': xca 'we (did)' + nao 'feel, know'. at ahau 'you, lord', as 011's Xca quizo, at ahau ('lord'). mi na re xcuyu ca he is doubtful: mi na re is read 'not even' after Brasseur ('On n'a même pas épargné nos queues'; a guess), and cuyu as 'bear, spare' (the cuyu 'hold back' of 015; inferred). ca he 'our tails' (he 'tail'): the birds speak of themselves.

sentences.t: Catepuch xhix qui chi, qui tohbal qui chahin chi elecaxic.
sentences.l: Then-also it-was-split their-mouths, their-payment their-guarding (chi) being-stolen.
sentences.i: Then their mouths were split open, as payment for their watch, in which the flowers were stolen.
sentences.n: Catepuch 'then also'. xhix qui chi 'their mouths were split' (Brasseur 'on leur fendit les lèvres'): hix is taken as 'split', a verb with no doer named (inferred; toggle xjix). qui tohbal 'their payment, punishment': toh 'pay' + -bal (inferred; toggle tojb'al). qui chahin 'their guarding' (chah 'guard' + -in, inferred). chi elecaxic 'with the stealing', the reason (Brasseur 'pour les châtier d'avoir laissé voler ce qui était commis à leur garde').

sentences.t: Quehe cut qui chacatahic Huncame, Vvcub Came cumal Hunahpu, Xbalanque, v xe ri banoh ri.
sentences.l: Thus then their-being-brought-low Huncame, Vucub Came by-them Hunahpu, Xbalanque, its-root the deed that.
sentences.i: This is how Huncame and Vucub Came were brought low by Hunahpu and Xbalanque; that was the beginning of what they did.
sentences.n: qui chacatahic 'their being brought low', the verbal noun, as in 009 and 014. v xe 'its root, its beginning' (xe 'root', as in the book's first line). ri banoh ri 'that deed': banoh 'doing, deed' (ban 'do' + -oh); ri … ri 'the … that'. Brasseur: 'ce fut là le commencement de leurs travaux' (inferred).

sentences.t: Ta xqui cam ri qui chi herebac qui chi Purpuec, herebac vacamic.
sentences.l: Then they-received the their-mouths split(?), their-mouths Purpuec, split(?) now.
sentences.i: So it was that they got their split mouths, the split mouths of the Purpuec, split to this day.
sentences.n: xqui cam 'they took, received' (cam 'take', with plain c; toggle xk'am). herebac 'split' (inferred, from xhix above; Brasseur herebak 'fendue'; toggle by the letters). qui chi Purpuec 'the mouths of the Purpuec': a bird, the Xpurpuvec of the call (¶6), written here without x- and with u for v. Brasseur's note: one watchman becomes a night bird called Purpuek, the other a kind of owl; 'aujourd'hui le premier se prononce Parpuak' (the birds are not otherwise identified). vacamic 'now, today': the story explains a bird's split beak. The name is kept.

sentences.t: Cate chi cut ta xcah chaah; xavi xere hunam que chaahic.
sentences.l: Then again then when it-went-down the-play; just so equal they-are-playing.
sentences.i: After that the game began again, and they played just as before, evenly matched.
sentences.n: Cate chi cut 'then again then' (chi is chic; toggle chik). xcah chaah 'the game went down', began, as in ¶1. xavi xere 'just so'. hunam que chaahic 'equally they play': hunam 'equal, alike', que, c- + e 'they', chaahic 'playing' (Brasseur 'ils jouèrent de même tous ensemble').

sentences.t: Xqueleh chi cu chaah, ta xe pixaban chi cu quib zacaric chic, xeꜭha Xibalba.
sentences.l: They-left-off(?) again then the-play, when they-counselled again then themselves at-dawn next, they-said Xibalba.
sentences.i: They left off (?) playing, and agreed among themselves on the next morning, so Xibalba said.
sentences.n: xqueleh 'they left off, ended (?)': not otherwise known (perhaps x- + qu- + eleh; Brasseur 'ayant achevé de jouer', at the end 'en terminant'; inferred; toggle xkelej by the letters). chi cu is chic + cu, twice (Brasseur chicu). xe pixaban quib 'they counselled one another', as in ¶3. zacaric chic 'at dawn next', the next morning (018's zacaric). xeꜭha Xibalba is left as a tag of the narrative ('so Xibalba said'), as Brasseur, though no quotation stands before it: it is Xibalba that sets the day.

sentences.t: “Vꜩ bala,” xeꜭha ꜭaholab, ta xqueleh.
sentences.l: “Good bala,” they-said the-boys, when they-left-off(?).
sentences.i: “Very well,” said the boys, and so they left off (?).
sentences.n: ta xqueleh 'when they left off', as above (inferred). The next part begins with the boys going into the next house of trial (Brasseur's tenth chapter).
